title: Priority Pass: Time-anchored Admission for Escalations and Cross-team Hedging
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Implement a time-anchored admission lane ("Priority Pass") for top-account escalations that guarantees bounded review turnaround and a deterministic fallback hedging policy across product, eng, and support. The goal is to reduce decision latency for VIP asks, limit unplanned roadmap churn, and create measurable SLAs for escalations so engineering can plan capacity without ad-hoc interrupts.
problem_statement: We receive high-urgency feature requests and escalation asks from top accounts that bypass standard intake and create unpredictable sprint churn. Current heuristics (ad-hoc prioritization, manual slack) are noisy, lack a temporal admission budget, and don't provide cross-team hedges when capacity is constrained. This causes missed SLAs, frustrated account teams, and unclear trade-offs for PM/Eng.
proposed_solution: Introduce 'Priority Pass' tokens that grant a time-anchored admission window (1-3 sprints) per top account per quarter, backed by: (1) a token budget calculator tied to capacity forecasts, (2) explicit acceptance criteria and deliverable templates, (3) a fallback hedging policy (defer + scoped workaround or funded POE) and (4) automation in the intake console to show pass status, remaining tokens, and expected delivery window.
acceptance_criteria: Design and API for Priority Pass visible in Console intake flow and account summary
Token budget calculator integrated with Dedicated capacity forecast and console capacity widget
Policy doc that enumerates acceptance criteria, fallback options (defer/scoped ship/handoff to solutions engineering), and SLA timelines published to GTM
Canary run with 3 pilot accounts showing reduced decision latency vs baseline (goal: 60% reduction in intake-to-decision median)
Automated dashboard displaying token spend, decision latency, and backlog churn metrics
metrics: % of VIP requests resolved within admission window (target: 85%)
Sprint churn attributable to VIP ad-hoc requests (target: -40%)
# of Priority Pass tokens used per quarter vs budget
Customer satisfaction NPS delta for pilot accounts
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (2 weeks): Policy drafting, stakeholder alignment, and token budget formula (PM + Finance + Eng infra)
Phase 1 (4 weeks): UX for intake + account console, backend token allocation service prototype, and observability hooks
Phase 2 (4 weeks): Pilot with 3 top accounts, run for 6 weeks, collect metrics and qualitative feedback
Phase 3 (2 weeks): Iterate policy and automation based on pilot, expand to 10 accounts and enable opt-in for enterprise customers
Phase 4 (ongoing): Bake into SLA and renewal playbooks; quarterly recalibration of token budgets
risks: Over-allocation of tokens leading to unrealistic delivery expectations
Top accounts gaming the system to reserve tokens for low-impact asks
Insufficient backend visibility causing token accounting divergence
Cross-team disputes on what constitutes a valid Priority Pass acceptance criteria
mitigations: Quarterly token budget reviews with Finance and GTM
Require a lightweight business-impact rubric on each intake to qualify for token spend
Distributed token ledger with reconciliation job and alerts for drift
Escalation adjudicator group (PM + Eng + CSM) for disputed cases with auto-escalation SLA
dependencies_notes: Relies on ENG-18722 (capacity forecast API) for token budget and ENG-19055 (console intake hook) for UI surface. Finance needs to provide historical ARR-to-feature weight mapping to seed the budget calculator.
